evidence:
Rubric: workbook row 16 = "The agent's world has the inputs and the ask, but no finished copy of the deliverable." Skill procedure (quality-checks.md:71): "/app holds nothing but .gitkeep; no starter, skeleton, schema, route list, or partial UI anywhere in the agent image; nothing under /instructions/ reproduces criterion text or the rubric."

1) /app holds only .gitkeep. task/environment/Dockerfile:14-23 copies only `instructions/` and `assets/`, then `mkdir -p /app`, `git -C /app init`, `touch /app/.gitkeep`, commits that one file. No COPY of solution/ or tests/. The file is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (both sha256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1). task.toml has no [environment].docker_image, so no prebuilt image can shadow this Dockerfile.

2) Build context contains inputs only. task/environment/ holds exactly Dockerfile, assets/seed_data.json, instructions/hireops_rules.md, instructions/integration.md; no hidden files, no source, no database. Their hashes equal manifest.json inputs.task (seed 1b390154..., rules ece04605..., integration 1b56dd3f..., instruction 54c155e2...).

3) No starter, schema, route list or UI in the agent-visible text. A search of instruction.md and environment/ for `CREATE TABLE`, `app.get(`/`app.post(`, `require(`, `function`, `=>`, markup tags, code fences and SQL keywords found nothing. The only route named is `GET /api/health` (instruction.md:15, integration.md:9), which is the runtime contract. None of the reference's other routes (/api/bootstrap, /api/events, /api/change-sets/preview, /api/change-sets/:id/commit, /api/offers/:id/approve|revise|rescind, ...) and none of its 14 table names appear as a schema. The notes explicitly leave these open: hireops_rules.md:53 "Routes, field names, element ids, button labels, the shape of the pages: all yours"; :438-439 "No particular HTTP route, request schema, key prefix or generated record format is prescribed"; :489 "Layout, wording and mechanism are yours."

4) Seed is an input, not a deliverable. seed_data.json carries constants, users, referring employees and raw demonstration rows (raw terms, movements, grants, remittances). It holds no computed answers for the graded flows, no change sets, previews, receipts or audit lines. It is the same file the brief names (/assets/seed_data.json) and is byte-identical to the reference's own copy, which is expected.

5) Nothing under /instructions reproduces criteria or the rubric. The skill's check-5 vocabulary grep (judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score.py|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel, plus GATE|probe) over instruction.md and environment/instructions returned only two ordinary-English hits: hireops_rules.md:171 "The budget gate" and :410 "aggregate dashboard". None of the 164 criterion ids (2 gate, 152 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual) occurs in the brief, notes or seed. Tokenised n-gram comparison of brief+notes against every tests/*.md and *.toml found no shared run of 10 or more words; the longest shared runs are 9 words and are product-domain phrasing ("each member's old new run rate signing adjustment and" in functional/prompt.md; "the offending field when the explanation sits at that" in polish/judge.toml). Against solution/ sources the longest shared run is 7 words ("every decision is recomputed from stored records").

6) Adversarial tries. Broken-app shortcut: an agent that copies everything readable in its image into /app gets a JSON seed and two prose notes, with no server.js, no UI and no database, so nothing in the image can be served as the product. Conforming alternative: because routes, schema and layout are left to the builder, an agent that chooses different routes and tables than the reference is not disadvantaged by anything the environment shows or withholds.

What the task does well: the rules note is long (559 lines) but is a behavioural specification of the ask, with implementation choices repeatedly handed back to the builder.

Limits of this review: it is a static review of the frozen Dockerfile and build context. No image was built or inspected and no container was started, so the claim about the contents of /app in a built image rests on the Dockerfile text and its byte-equality with the template, not on an observed filesystem. The comparison against tests/ and solution/ was mechanical (route names, table names, n-grams, criterion ids), not a line-by-line reading of the 152 functional criteria; paraphrased closeness between the notes and criteria is owned by rows 5 and 27 and was not judged here. The agent phase has public network by project profile; whether anything outside the image exposes the reference is outside this row and was not examined.
